gaps: No supported climate-to-violence or reverse-FCV pathway was identified. Relocation and disaster evacuation do not by themselves establish FCV.
The four-city assessment uses 2011 census inputs and qualitative capacity review; it is preliminary, and flood/drainage areas were not hydrologically recalculated for future maps.
IMF national economic and relocation findings must not be assigned equally to named study departments. Model shock responses are not calendar forecasts.

The SINAE annual page contains an aggregate inconsistency; only identified event or flood-row figures are retained. Event counts and official response accounts are not independent outcome evaluations.

executive_assessment.text: Four named urban study areas provide census-block vulnerability factors; the Juan Lacaze sewer finding is historical, not a statement about current service coverage.
Severe drought affected national agricultural output, while modeled macroeconomic responses and historical relocation evidence have distinct scales and denominators.
Named Paysandú/Salto sites and 2023–2024 flood events document evacuation and service pressures. SATI preparedness is a capacity; neither relocation nor evacuation proves violence.
